rules.reason: a shipment is the operator's own paperwork about their own goods; no delete, because a parcel that went out cannot be made not to have gone out -- a mistake is a lost/returned status or an inbound shipment, never a vanished row
the lines are the shipment; same scope and the same no-delete posture, and the over-shipping gate in hook_shipment_lines runs on this path whoever the caller is
packing is warehouse work, not owner-only work: anybody signed in can raise a shipment, and everything they can put in it is bounded by what the order already committed to

operator-facing, deliberately NOT public: the slip is addressed by an internal shipment id, so a public page here would be an enumeration oracle for every parcel in the shop. The customer's door is the payment portal's capability token, which is unguessable and revocable; a slip is printed by the person holding the box
the picker has to be signed in for the page to know whose warehouse to fold; the page itself shows a sign-in prompt rather than an error to anyone who is not
